title: How YdBB’s members shape a song together
description: “LETTER” and “Voyage” reveal the work behind a shared arrangement credit, from fitting a guitar solo to a melody to directing and editing vocals.

blocks.text: YdBB’s singles compilation YdBB 1.25 gathers songs released between their first and second albums, including “Voyage” (항해). Retailer Dope Records schedules the vinyl release for November 26, 2026. It offers an occasion to revisit how the five members divide the work of making a song. [Compilation listing](https://www.doperecord.com/product/예약판매-유다빈밴드-ydbb-ydbb-125-180g-black-vinyl/7639/category/1/display/2/?icid=MAIN.product_listmain_1).

On their 2021 debut album, “LETTER” credits vocalist Yu Dabin with lyrics and composition, and YdBB with arrangement. Guitarist Lee Junhyung supplied one concrete explanation of that collective credit in IZM’s December 2024 interview: he shaped the guitar solo to suit the vocal melody. His account gives the instrumental passage a specific reference point—the tune being sung. [Album credits from Biscuit Sound](https://www.biscuitsound.net/index.php?document_srl=54372&mid=music); [IZM interview](https://www.izm.co.kr/posts?id=33059).

The writing responsibilities widened. Dabin told IZM that the first album began with her songwriting and the members helping arrange; other members subsequently began participating in lyrics and composition. “Voyage”, released on June 25, 2023, names all five under lyrics, composition and arrangement: Dabin, Junhyung, bassist Cho Youngyun, keyboardist You Myeongjong and drummer Lee Sangwoon. Those credits establish shared responsibility without specifying who first proposed each passage. [IZM interview](https://www.izm.co.kr/posts?id=33059); [“Voyage” release and credits](https://www.genie.co.kr/detail/albumInfo?axnm=83966841).

Youngyun’s explanation to IZM makes one decision clear: he deliberately left gaps in the “Voyage” bass line to give guitar and keyboards room. Sangwoon described the song as an example of his drumming growing in intensity, with almost no post-editing. These are different kinds of choices within the same recording: how much space a part occupies, and how a performance develops and is retained. [IZM interview](https://www.izm.co.kr/posts?id=33059).

The detailed credits also show work beyond the members’ principal instruments. Myeongjong receives piano and synthesizer, MIDI programming and vocal-directing credits. Youngyun is credited with bass, electric guitar alongside Junhyung, and vocal editing. For this recording, the keyboardist’s responsibilities reached into guiding the singing, while the bassist also worked on the recorded vocals. [“Voyage” production credits](https://www.genie.co.kr/detail/albumInfo?axnm=83966841).

Genie’s promotional report from the “Voyage” recording and mixing sessions describes members exchanging detailed feedback even on parts other than their own. Read alongside the credits, that account suggests a division of tasks with room for discussion across them. A member could have a named responsibility—bass, programming, vocal direction—while still helping another member decide what their part needed. [Genie’s session report](https://www.genie.co.kr/magazine/subMain?ctid=1&mgz_seq=13299); [recording credits](https://www.genie.co.kr/detail/albumInfo?axnm=83966841).
